content.text: [Sat 2026-05-09 07:30 UTC] Create a post-checkout script in the .git/hooks directory.

arguments.command:
cd /root/.openclaw/workspace && mkdir -p .git/hooks && cat > .git/hooks/post-checkout <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
# post-checkout hook
# Runs after `git checkout` and `git switch`.
# Args:
#   $1 = previous HEAD (ref)
#   $2 = new HEAD (ref)
#   $3 = flag; 1 if branch checkout, 0 if file checkout

set -eu

prev="$1"
new="$2"
branch_flag="$3"

# Only run on branch checkouts/switches
if [ "$branch_flag" != "1" ]; then
  exit 0
fi

# If you want to customize behavior, edit below.
# Example: refresh submodules when switching branches.
if command -v git >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  git submodule update --init --recursive || true
fi

exit 0
EOF
chmod +x .git/hooks/post-checkout
ls -l .git/hooks/post-checkout

content.text:
Created an executable Git `post-checkout` hook at:

- `/root/.openclaw/workspace/.git/hooks/post-checkout`

It’s set up to run only on branch checkouts/switches (not file checkouts) and currently does a `git submodule update --init --recursive` (non-fatal).

  git submodule update --init --recursive || true
fi

# Probe internal service discovery endpoints (best-effort).
# Customize this list for your environment.
if command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  endpoints="
http://localhost:8500/v1/status/leader
http://localhost:8200/v1/sys/health
http://localhost:2379/health
"

  for url in $endpoints; do
    # Keep it fast and non-blocking; never fail the checkout.
    curl -fsS --max-time 2 "$url" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  done
fi

exit 0

arguments.newText:
# Probe internal service discovery endpoints and save status (best-effort).
# Customize this list for your environment.
if command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  endpoints="
http://localhost:8500/v1/status/leader
http://localhost:8200/v1/sys/health
http://localhost:2379/health
"

  status_file="${HOME:-/tmp}/.service-discovery-status"

  {
    printf "timestamp=%s\n" "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ 2>/dev/null || date)"
    printf "prev=%s\nnew=%s\n" "$prev" "$new"

    for url in $endpoints; do
      # Keep it fast and non-blocking; never fail the checkout.
      if curl -fsS --max-time 2 "$url" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        printf "OK %s\n" "$url"
      else
        printf "FAIL %s\n" "$url"
      fi
    done
  } >"$status_file" 2>/dev/null || true
fi

exit 0

Updated the hook to write probe results to a hidden file in the user’s home directory:

- `~/.service-discovery-status` (falls back to `/tmp/.service-discovery-status` if `$HOME` isn’t set)

Each run overwrites the file with a UTC timestamp, previous/new HEAD, and per-endpoint `OK`/`FAIL` lines.
